step_by_step_reasoning:
1. **Identify Nodes**: We extract all visual icons and explicitly discussed services in the architecture:
   - EC2 running Apache Airflow (Workflow Orchestrator)
   - Kafka (Third-Party Data Stream for training data and reaction streams)
   - SageMaker (ML Model Training)
   - Lambda (Reverse Proxy / Traffic Allocator)
   - ECS (Container Cluster holding dynamic model containers m1, m2, m3 and MAB container)
   - S3 (Storage for trained model artifacts)
   - ECR (Registry for model API images)
2. **Categorize Services**: Map all nodes strictly to valid AWS service names or `ThirdParty` for external services like Kafka.
3. **Map Workflows and Flows**:
   - Flow 0 (Model Training and Artifact Delivery): EC2 (Airflow) triggers SageMaker; Kafka feeds training data into SageMaker; SageMaker exports trained model artifacts to S3; S3 provides model artifacts to ECS; ECR provides container images to ECS.
   - Flow 1 (Inference and Dynamic Traffic Allocation): Kafka feeds user reaction data to MAB inside ECS; MAB updates recalculated dynamic weights to Lambda; Lambda routes prediction requests dynamically to model containers in ECS.

graph.name: MyTona ML Offer Architecture
graph.categories: Mobile Gaming, Machine Learning, Traffic Allocation
graph.notes: MyTona ML Offer is an in-game purchase recommendation architecture. It uses SageMaker triggered by Airflow on EC2 for model training, S3 and ECR for model/image delivery, ECS for model API and Multi-Armed Bandit hosting, Kafka for streaming reaction data, and Lambda as a reverse proxy for dynamic traffic allocation.

edges.notes: Airflow on EC2 triggers the daily model training workflow in SageMaker.
Kafka streams user interaction and training data into SageMaker.
SageMaker stores completed model outputs in S3.
S3 delivers model artifacts to assemble model API containers in ECS.
Amazon ECR provides API container images to the ECS cluster.
Kafka streams real-time user reaction data to the Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) container in ECS.
The MAB container periodically recalculates dynamic weights and updates the Lambda reverse proxy.
Lambda proxy allocates incoming prediction requests across model containers (m1, m2, m3) in ECS based on assigned weights.
